<h1 align="center">Castaway</h1>

<p align="center">
  <b>A 10-hour lo-fi island video in which almost nothing happens.<br>
  This is normal. No action is required.</b><br>
  <sub>working title &middot; unofficial, inspired by the 1992 screensaver <i>Johnny Castaway</i> &middot; 16:9, 1080p, 30 fps &middot; always daytime</sub>
</p>

One young woman, one tall palm, one raft and a great deal of time. She stands on a very small island with her headphones on, nodding to the music, and every so often something happens: a drone delivers a parcel that turns out to be more headphones, a coconut lands on a hermit crab and the crab walks off wearing it, and the bottle she throws out to sea comes straight back. Then nothing happens for a while, which is the main feature.

It is built like the 10-hour lo-fi streams: one fixed shot, and **more than 90 activities** in [`activities.toml`](activities.toml), on four timers plus chained follow-ups. Each one waits for the next bar of the music (every 3 seconds), so the gags land on the beat. **Every sound is synthesized from code** by [`tools/make_audio.py`](tools/make_audio.py): no samples, no borrowed loops, no recordings, so no third-party licence applies.

**Run it**, then open <a href="http://127.0.0.1:8765/">http://127.0.0.1:8765/</a> for the live preview and the export to a YouTube-ready MP4:

```sh
python tools/serve.py
```

<p><sub>The desktop in the banner is a drawing, but the clock under the preview really counts: it starts at 2:47:03 when the page opens and wraps at 10:00:00, which is how long a run lasts. Please do not restart your computer.</sub></p>

<details>
<summary><b>Gags</b>: found new hardware, and other notifications</summary>

```text
┌─ Event Viewer: Island ───────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                                                                          │
│  Type          Source      Description                                   │
│  ───────────   ─────────   ─────────────────────────────────────────     │
│  Information   bottle      Message returned to sender, at once. Hours    │
│                            later a different bottle brings a reply.      │
│  Information   drone       New hardware delivered: headphones, one       │
│                            more pair. Later, the tide takes the box.     │
│  Warning       coconut     Fell on a hermit crab. The crab now lives     │
│                            in it, and has left, wearing it.              │
│  Information   turtle      A sea turtle visited.                         │
│  Information   cat         Stray cat (grey tabby, white chest) came      │
│                            on a crate, climbed the palm, napped. One     │
│                            day it floats off again. It comes back.       │
│  Warning       signal      One bar, available at the top of the palm.    │
│  Information   shark       Audio device found: a shark, wearing          │
│                            headphones, nodding to the beat.              │
│  Information   tour boat   Passengers took selfies. Boat left.           │
│  Information   her         Walked out over the water. Came back with     │
│                            an iced coffee. She could leave any time.     │
│  Information   hydrofoil   A bro on an electric hydrofoil waved a        │
│                            shaka and carved off.                         │
│  Information   bushcraft   Fire by friction, a hammock, a lookout up     │
│                            the palm, spear fishing.                      │
│  Information   kumara      Planted. Grows over the course of the video.  │
│  Information   routine     Coconut sipped. Fish attempted. Laps jogged.  │
│                            Rescue waved for. Sandcastle built.           │
│  Information   tide        Sandcastle removed.                           │
│                                                                          │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

Underneath all of it runs the scene's own life: shore waves and drifting cloud shadows are built; distant birds, planes with vapour trails, whale pods, dolphins, sailboats, sandpipers, a gecko and a rain shower are planned.

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>Schedule</b>: four timers, one beat</summary>

```text
┌─ Scheduled Tasks ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                                                                          │
│  Task          Runs                         In a 10-hour run             │
│  ───────────   ──────────────────────────   ──────────────────────       │
│  regular       every 2 to 5 minutes         about 155                    │
│  occasional    every 12 to 25 minutes       about 30                     │
│  rare          every 30 to 60 minutes       about 13                     │
│  super rare    every 3 to 6 hours           about 2, never over 3        │
│  chained       when another task says so    about 20 follow-ups          │
│                                                                          │
│  Start at .... the next bar of the music (one bar is 3 seconds)          │
│  Run for ..... 10:00:00                 Seed ...... 1992                 │
│  Busy ........ about a third of the time. Idle: the rest of it.          │
│                                                                          │
│  [x] Let lanes overlap (a ship may pass while she is busy)               │
│  [x] Run only in daytime                                                 │
│  [ ] Stop the task if it runs for more than 10 hours                     │
│                                                                          │
│                                [   OK   ]  [ Cancel ]  [ Apply ]         │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

Counts are medians of 200 simulated 10-hour runs, from the header of [`activities.toml`](activities.toml). Same seed, same schedule, event for event. Lanes are why things can overlap: she has one, and the cat, the turtle, the sea and sky, the shore and the kumara patch each have their own. [`python tools/schedule.py`](tools/schedule.py) validates the file and simulates a run.

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>Sound</b>: every sound is synthesized from code</summary>

```text
┌─ Sounds and Audio Devices ───────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                                                                          │
│  ♪ theme      a seamless 60-second loop at 80 BPM in F major,            │

│  = mix        -14 LUFS, true peak at or below -1 dBTP; levels set        │

│  Source ..... tools/make_audio.py, more than 150 files                   │
│  Samples .... none   Borrowed loops ... none   Recordings ... none       │
│  Heard by ... nobody yet. Listening is on the schedule; tier unknown.    │
│                                                                          │
│  Volume  ├──────────────────────────────█────────┤   [ ] Mute            │
│                                                                          │
│                                           [   OK   ]  [ Cancel ]         │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

All of it comes out of [`tools/make_audio.py`](tools/make_audio.py). No samples, no borrowed loops, no recordings, so no third-party licence applies.

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>Run it</b>: the tools you will actually use</summary>

- [`python tools/serve.py`](tools/serve.py), then <a href="http://127.0.0.1:8765/">http://127.0.0.1:8765/</a>: the renderer ([`web/index.html`](web/index.html)), with a live preview and frame-exact export in the browser (WebCodecs H.264, 68 to 78 frames a second at 1080p30 in Chrome). The server mixes the sound and joins the two into an MP4. Plain ES modules, no build step, no npm packages.
- [`python tools/schedule.py`](tools/schedule.py): validates the schedule and simulates a 10-hour run.
- [`python tools/render_demo.py --dev`](tools/render_demo.py): a dev reel of every activity with a heads-up display, from the older Python reference renderer.
- [`tools/make_audio.py`](tools/make_audio.py): where every sound comes from.

Hard cuts and stepped movement are the motion defaults. The working notes are in [`MUSING.md`](MUSING.md).

</details>
